To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the energy pumped into a semiflexible chain under the action of a spatially homogeneous periodic external field is localized on the places where the chain has a smaller radius of curvature.
(1) the shape of the chain is determined by the competition between the driving and the damping forces and (2) the energy is localized in those parts of the chain where the chain is flat.
The dynamics of the driven and damped chain is determined by the competition between two factors: the driving force and damping, and the coupling between the internal and bending degrees of freedom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of molecular rings in a spatially homogeneous time-dependent external field.
the dynamics of semiflexible polymer rings under external forcing.
energy localization and shape transformations of semiflexible polymer rings under external periodic driving.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the localization of the excitations in semiflexible polymer molecules is a generic feature, and that it is not restricted to the case of a flat surface, but can be found in the case of a spherical surface as well.
in the presence of a spatially homogeneous time-dependent field a closed ring of molecular subunits undergoes a nonequilbrium phase transition and the shape of the ring becomes unstable.
in the case of the semiflexible polymer rings, the energy localization and the shape transformations in driven and/or damped molecular chains is possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shape of a driven and damped chain is determined by a balance between the driving, the dissipation, the bending rigidity and the coupling between the internal and the bending degrees.
the shape of a driven semiflexible polymer ring depends on the excitation energy.
the shape of the ring depends on the excitation energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in a driven and damped semiflexible chain the shape transformations can be triggered by the energy pumping into the system.
the shape of the ring depends on the energy distribution in the system.
the shape of a semiflexible chain is not only a function of its internal degrees of freedom but also of external driving.
